rationale: The hypothesis posits that cerebellar atrophy severity in TUBA4A-associated spastic ataxia (SPAX11) is dictated by variant position and biochemical disruption rather than disease duration, proposing that de novo catalytic-core variants systematically cause rapid, severe pancerebellar atrophy (<5 years) while C-terminal inherited variants progress indolently. Current literature partially supports the general phenotypic divergence: Torella et al. (2023) demonstrated that patients carrying the C-terminal p.Glu415Lys variant exhibit spastic ataxia with slight or absent cerebellar atrophy even across extended disease courses, whereas Benkirane et al. (2024) linked several de novo missense variants to marked microtubule dynamic defects and severe cerebellar atrophy. However, the strict hypothesis is contradicted and unproven in several critical respects: (1) Johari et al. (2026) described a de novo N-terminal/core variant (p.Gln11His) resulting in mild rather than accelerated pancerebellar atrophy, directly conflicting with the claim that all de novo core mutations cause accelerated pancerebellar atrophy within 5 years; (2) systematic semi-quantitative atrophy scoring matched strictly for disease duration across cohorts has not been formally conducted; and (3) clinical expression displays variable age of onset and incomplete penetrance without a verified strict five-year temporal threshold.

evidence.text: Benkirane et al. identified ultra-rare TUBA4A missense variants in spastic ataxia, reporting 12 patients presenting with spasticity and/or cerebellar ataxia (including 5 confirmed de novo cases and a previously reported familial mutation). Patient-derived fibroblasts demonstrated significant structural alterations in microtubule organization and dynamics, with de novo cases exhibiting prominent cerebellar atrophy.

source.quote: In the present study, we report two families, one with 11 affected individuals and the other with a single patient, carrying a novel, likely pathogenic, variant (p. Glu415Lys) in the TUBA4A gene (NM_006000)... Brain MRI showed slight or absent cerebellar atrophy.

evidence.text: Johari et al. documented that de novo TUBA4A missense variants can manifest as myo-tubulinopathies with skeletal myopathy and mild cerebellar atrophy rather than rapid, severe pancerebellar atrophy, demonstrating that de novo mutations outside the C-terminus do not uniformly cause accelerated pancerebellar neurodegeneration.

evidence.text: Hines et al. established a dominant mouse model harboring Tuba4a p.Gln176Pro, showing that a specific core structural mutation leads to rapid Purkinje cell degeneration and spastic ataxia beginning between 22 and 30 days, confirming that intrinsic structural mutations can selectively trigger rapid cerebellar degeneration, but also highlighting co-occurring myogenic pathology.

conflicts: The hypothesis asserts that all de novo catalytic-core variants trigger rapid pancerebellar atrophy within <5 years, whereas Johari et al. identified de novo core mutations associated with only mild cerebellar atrophy or predominant skeletal myo-tubulinopathy.

No prospective or retrospective cohort has formally applied standardized semi-quantitative cerebellar atrophy scales matched directly by disease duration between C-terminal (p.Glu415Lys) and catalytic-core cohorts.

Variable penetrance and broad ranges of onset age in both inherited and de novo TUBA4A cases indicate that disease duration and genetic background contribute alongside intrinsic biophysical disruption.

new_directions.question_text: Do longitudinal volumetric MRI cerebellar analyses distinguish rate of cerebellar volume loss between p.Glu415Lys and catalytic-core TUBA4A mutations after adjusting for disease duration?
new_directions.rationale: Directly testing volumetric loss per year across genotype groups will settle whether variant location independently determines neurodegenerative tempo or if indolent atrophy is an artifact of ascertainment.

new_directions.question_text: How do tubulin polymerization dynamics and MAP/motor protein interaction kinetics differ biochemically between p.Glu415Lys and central globular core variants in vitro?
new_directions.rationale: Measuring in vitro microtubule catastrophe, polymerization rates, and kinesin motility will elucidate whether C-terminal modifications selectively preserve polymerization while altering transport.
